sections.html:
Just west of Boston and Cambridge, Watertown is a compact Middlesex County city first settled in 1630. Its 35,329 residents (2020 census) share about four square miles, 4.12 in total, or roughly 8,840 per square mile. A council-manager government runs the city, and a November 2021 vote made "The City of Watertown" the official name. ZIP code: 02472.

The Charles River marks much of the southern and eastern edge, facing Boston's Brighton neighborhood. Belmont sits to the north, Newton to the south, Cambridge to the east and Waltham to the west. Neighborhood names you will hear in listings include Bemis, Coolidge Square, East Watertown, Watertown Square and the West End.

Some Watertown lots have carried buildings for nearly four centuries. Many owners hold houses from the streetcar-suburb era, and buyers of those homes ask how old the roof, wiring and heating are.

The Watertown Arsenal made military armaments from 1816 until 1995, when the Army sold the site. It has since turned into offices, shops, restaurants and the Mosesian Center for the Arts. Arsenal Yards and the Watertown Mall now face each other along Arsenal Street, and the Arsenal campus was bought by Alexandria Real Estate Equities in 2019, adding life science development nearby. Boston and Cambridge are right next door, so many residents commute out.

East Watertown is home to a large Armenian community, with churches, newspapers and grocery stores concentrated there.

Bus service runs through Watertown Square and Watertown Yard, and the Massachusetts Turnpike and Soldiers Field Road run along the edges toward downtown Boston. The Green Line's A branch once reached the city but stopped in 1969.

Three transport questions come up with most Watertown buyers:

  • How far is the nearest MBTA bus stop?
  • How long is the drive to the Pike or Soldiers Field Road at rush hour?
  • Is there off-street parking, which is scarce on tight city lots?

Answer them in the listing text. A cash buyer planning to renovate cares far less.

About 2,600 students attend Watertown's public schools: three elementary schools, a middle school and Watertown High School. Private choices include the Perkins School, St. Stephen's Armenian Elementary School and the Atrium School. Family buyers often begin with schools, so keep the list ready.

Watertown taxes follow state law, and the Appellate Tax Board publishes a public guide to contesting a bill. The valuation date is January 1 ahead of the fiscal year, which means the fiscal 2025 bill is based on what the house was worth on January 1, 2024.

Cities on a quarterly schedule usually send installments due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, while a twice-a-year city typically sets the due date thirty days after the bill is mailed. Your bill shows which applies, and that matters because the abatement window is tied to the first installment.

  • Submit the abatement application to the local assessors by the first installment date, typically February 1 under quarterly billing.
  • The assessors have three calendar months to respond. If they stay silent, the request is treated as denied.
  • You then have three months to appeal to the Appellate Tax Board.
  • Keep paying on schedule, because the board will not hear a case with taxes in arrears.

The assessing office in Watertown can tell you its current calendar and give you the abatement form.

Sellers in Massachusetts normally pay the deed excise tax, set at $2.28 for each $500 of the price or any fraction of $500. Put another way, it is $4.56 per $1,000. G.L. c. 64D, section 1 creates the tax and exempts deeds where a city, town or the state is a party.

Watertown deeds are recorded in Middlesex County, and the registry there posts its own fee schedule. Your closing attorney can give you the exact recording charge and tell you how the excise is to be paid.

sections.h2: Questions to put to city offices
sections.html:
City rules shift, so verify a few things with the offices themselves, ideally before you list or sign a purchase agreement:

  • Does the property have open permits, violations or unpaid municipal charges?
  • Is any inspection or certificate required for a sale or a change in occupancy?
  • If tenants live there, which notice and registration rules apply?
  • When are the tax installments on your current bill due?

Loose ends slow a conventional sale and can lower what a buyer will pay. A buyer paying cash for an as-is house will often take it with such items still open, and the price will account for them.

sections.h2: Choosing between a listing, a private sale and cash
sections.html:
A listing exposes the house to the largest group of buyers, though it generally brings repairs, showings and a closing date driven by the buyer's lender. A cash sale moves faster and with less fuss, and its price usually reflects the work needed.

When you are dealing with an inherited house, an empty property, tenants or put-off repairs, set the net from a listing, after commission, repairs and the weeks of carrying costs, beside a written cash offer. Read any contract closely before you sign.

In a cash sale, you share the address and condition, the buyer looks over the property and any liens or taxes, and an offer follows. If you accept, an attorney or title company prepares the paperwork and the closing date is set around your timeline. You can say no and keep your options open.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes are owed
sections.html: Selling with an unpaid tax bill or a lien is common. Whatever is owed is paid off from the sale proceeds at closing, and your attorney or title company works out the amounts. Call the assessing office and your lender for payoff figures before you accept an offer so you know what you will actually keep.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to keys
sections.html:
1. Gather your latest tax bill and any papers on permits, tenants or repairs.
  2. Ask the city offices the questions above.
  3. Choose your route and compare written offers.
  4. Hire your attorney, who coordinates the deed and recording in Middlesex County.
  5. Close, pay off taxes and liens from proceeds, and hand over the keys.

A cash sale shortens this list because there is no lender approval to wait on and no round of showings. Keep copies of everything you sign, and ask the attorney to explain each closing line before the day arrives.

faqs.q: Is Watertown, MA a city or a town?
faqs.a: A city. Voters changed the official name to "The City of Watertown" in November 2021, and it has a council-manager government.
The city covers about 4.12 square miles and had 35,329 residents at the 2020 census.

faqs.q: How much is the deed excise tax when I sell a house in Watertown?
faqs.a: $2.28 per $500 of the sale price, rounded up for any fraction of $500. The seller usually pays it at recording.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Watertown property tax assessment?
faqs.a: Apply to the assessors before the first installment date on your bill. If you disagree with the result, you have three months to appeal to the state Appellate Tax Board. Keep paying on time meanwhile.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Watertown house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Options include listing it as is, selling to an investor, or taking a cash offer from a company that buys houses as is. Taxes and liens owed get paid from your proceeds at closing.
